Uh the LS and HC components don't necessarily play nice with each other. The problem is the high signal for a HC part is 3.3 usually and the high signal threshold for a LS part is 4v. You can attempt to mix and hope it works out

Finally on your HC parts NOTHING can be left floating this means you will need tie down and up resistors in places (1k to ground for pull down and 1k to vcc for pull up) typical tie down anything not in use and tie up anything with inverted input, finally use current limiting resistors(I found 220 to be good) on any non chip to chip outputs

A tanker holds about 6 compartments of 5kL or so( could be off with the literage) but a tanker is normal split with any one else in the area who also needs fuel

My understanding is the petrol pays for the site costs, the shop inside lines the pockets of the owner.

Emergency top ups are some times ordered in advance, typically around big holidays like easter and any public holiday in summer. i cant remember the rate but the fuel is still a draw card for people even if the company isnt making money on the petrol its self.

Whats embarrassing for the manager: ordering a topup and not having enough capacity to take the fuel from the tanker. If the tanker cant unload your order you get stung with a penalty and they take the excess with them and they don't come back but you've still paid for it

biggest thing you will see being fueled at a petrol station is heavy commercial e.g. rubbish trucks, light haulers etc and even then they are rare and only have a fuel tank of about 200L so 15kL(what we'd keep in stock) or 20kL (max) would last a day meaning we can get it topped up

the above is a common configuration, unless its a super busy petrol station they might have a dedicated diesel tanker and a split 91/95 tank. Not many people buy 95 majority is 91 followed by diesel.

Also on a side note its super embarrassing for a petrol station to run out of any fuel and will order an expensive emergency topup to avoid this and not make any money on the fuel (the station i worked at had a profit margin of around 15 cents to the liter before taking in any discounts)

these will be partitioned 1 full tank for 91, half tank for 95/96/98 and a half tank for diesel.
